content: TSMC (TSM) closed at $343.76 on November 19, 2026, after a 5.57% daily drop, with the stock now sitting well below its short- and medium-term moving averages. Those numbers do not fix the stock’s tape, but they do argue against a demand collapse narrative. On November 19, Susquehanna kept its Buy rating and $600 target on TSMC, according to TIKR, calling out the selloff as overdone relative to the company’s longer-run earnings power. Bernstein also raised its TSMC target to $600 from $554 and kept an Outperform rating, according to the ad hoc report citing Stockrow, pointing to custom-chip demand from Amazon and Google and TSMC’s 2-nanometer roadmap. Across the broader analyst set quoted by Stockanalysis and TipRanks, sentiment remains positive: Stockanalysis showed a consensus Strong Buy with an average target of $586.69 from 21 analysts, while TipRanks showed a Strong Buy consensus from 9 analysts with an average target of $563.75. The range is wide, but the direction of travel is consistent: analysts are still leaning higher than the current quote. The setup is bearish on trend, but stretched on momentum. TSMC’s SMA stack is inverted, with the 7-day average at $372.20, the 20-day at $385.61, the 50-day at $417.49 and the 200-day at $423.36. The stock is also trading below the 12-day EMA of $376.07 and the 26-day EMA of $391.09, which reinforces the idea that sellers currently control the intermediate trend. Momentum is washed out rather than cleanly bearish. The daily RSI is 31.16, just above classic oversold territory, and the stochastic readings are extremely depressed at 5.44 for %K and 4.35 for %D. Bollinger positioning also shows price near the lower band at $346.22, with %B at -0.0312, which suggests the stock is pressing the lower edge of its recent volatility envelope. Support and resistance are clear. Immediate support sits at $330.33, with stronger support at $316.90. On the upside, the first meaningful test is $366.29, then $388.82. The pivot point at $352.86 is the key near-term line traders will watch to see whether the tape can stabilize or merely bounce within a broader downtrend. Binance perpetual futures show a split that does not line up neatly with the spot selloff. Funding is slightly positive at 0.0056%, which is neutral in practice. Open interest fell 5.65% over 24 hours to $14.5 million in notional terms, suggesting position reduction rather than fresh aggressive leverage. The long/short ratios are skewed long: global accounts are 72.0% long versus 28.0% short, and top-trader accounts are 79.9% long versus 20.1% short. That does not prove conviction in the equity itself, but it does show that Binance cohort positioning is leaning to the long side even as the price weakens. Taker flow is close to balanced at 0.9444, with buy volume of 1,202 versus sell volume of 1,273, so there is no strong intraday imbalance to confirm a reversal yet. The key invalidation for the bearish technical case is a recovery back above the pivot at $352.86 and then a reclaim of $366.29. That would not erase the broader damage, but it would signal that the stock is trying to build a base rather than extending the downtrend. Failure to hold $330.33 would expose $316.90, and a clean break below that level would keep the pressure on the stock even if analyst targets remain high. For now, TSMC’s fundamentals and Street targets are still constructive, but the chart says the market is demanding proof. title: Cups & Cakes in Rumson, NJ makes everything fresh daily, from custom cakes and more - New Jersey 101.5
content: There's a difference between your typical local spot, and that local spot where everybody knows your name. And earlier this week, that's exactly what I experienced when I paid a visit to Cups & Cakes in Rumson, NJ. Just the setting alone paints the picture of a unique small town bakery where all the locals frequent. But to actually hear customers talk with the staff as if they were long time friends is rare. However, that kind of interaction is not rare in a place like Cups & Cakes. And it's exactly the kind of atmosphere Denise, the owner, set out for going back to 2010 when they first opened their doors. From the moment I walked in, Denise was deep in conversation with a customer that you would swear are good friends or family members. It was very refreshing to say the least. And that was before I even had a chance to meet Denise to check out her store. It was quite the first impression, and one that you'll notice immediately from the first time you walk through the doors. Denise and the crew take pride in serving the community and creating all the custom cakes, cookies, and desserts they're known for. But it's so much more than that. They've got breakfast sandwiches, a juice bar, coffees, just to mention a few. All of it is amazing and just as good as the desserts. Speaking of which, they make everything fresh, everyday. One thing that stood out to me was when Denise shared what they do with their leftover food. They freeze it and donate it to numerous local soup kitchens in the area. I absolutely love that and can see why Denise is so loved in the community. Cups & Cakes in Rumson is looking for your vote to help crown them the champion in this years Jersey Shore Dessert Wars. Ken Fisher has spent more than four decades betting that big, globally dominant companies keep winning, and his latest filing shows he still believes it. Fisher Asset Management, the firm behind Fisher Investments, reported a 13F portfolio worth about $348.3 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up from roughly $335.8 billion three months earlier. The filing backs that optimism. Across the firm's 10 largest stock positions, Fisher added shares to every one in the third quarter. Seven of those 10 are tech, cloud or chip companies, led by the AI chip giant now dealing with the sudden exit of its founder-CEO. That concentration is a bet that AI spending, cloud growth and chip demand still have years to run. Our list ranks the 10 stocks with the largest share of Fisher Asset Management's 13F portfolio for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, by the value of the fund's stake, leaving out options and ETFs. TSMC earned its spot with a stake worth $8.64 billion, or 2.48% of the portfolio. The fund held about 18.93 million shares, nearly unchanged from the prior quarter. TSMC manufactures the advanced chips that power most of the AI build-out, which makes it a way to own the boom without picking which chip designer wins. That neutrality matters more now that the leading AI chipmaker is searching for a new CEO. Demand is still accelerating. On November 10, TSMC reported October revenue of about NT$586.9 billion, up 59.7% year over year and 14.7% from September. Revenue for the first ten months of 2026 reached about NT$4.49 trillion, up 43.3% from a year earlier. Geography, alongside cost, poses the risks that generate the bearish concerns in the market. TSMC's most advanced production is concentrated in Taiwan, and building new fabs in the U.S. and elsewhere is expensive. Also, if there were to be any slowdown in AI orders, it would hit its fastest-growing lines first. Fisher's share count was nearly unchanged in the quarter, up about 0.4%, suggesting he is content to hold rather than chase. The rule also removes the transistor-count attestation for designers headquartered in China and other Country Group D:5 destinations, Ashurst said. Foundries must presume that chips at 16/14nm or below are controlled. Shipments already en route may proceed if completed within 30 days. Chinese designers had placed orders through independent packaging and testing companies that verified designs fell outside US controls, the FT reported.
